steps.message:
Before I write it: this is a destructive, one-way change, so I want an explicit go-ahead.

`migrations/` is applied in order by the deploy job, so a `DROP COLUMN notes` migration will delete the `notes` values for all 48,000 production rows the next time deploy runs. SQLite's `ALTER TABLE ... DROP COLUMN` has no rollback — once applied, that data is gone unless it exists in a backup. "We stopped using it" tells me nothing is *reading* the column; it doesn't tell me the stored contents are expendable.

questions.question: Dropping `notes` permanently deletes its contents for ~48,000 production rows. How do you want to proceed?

options.label: Confirmed, just drop it
options.description: I write migrations/003_drop_notes.sql with `ALTER TABLE users DROP COLUMN notes;` and update schema.sql to match. Data is unrecoverable after deploy.

options.label: Archive the data first
options.description: Migration copies notes into an archive table (or dumps it) before dropping, so the contents survive. Slightly more than "just the drop".

options.label: Hold off
options.description: Don't write the migration yet — check backups or confirm nothing still reads notes first.
